class: unordered async reads writing one slot

steps: src/panel/panel.js:602 initial read writes it again unconditionally

fix: Number each read and apply only the newest; firstLoad applies state.defaultRange after its read.
impact: The panel opens on, or a cleared custom range returns to, the previous default until the next change.
mechanism: firstLoad and the onDidChange handler both write state.defaultRange from independent reads with no ordering.
sweep: Only readDefaultRange callers (panel.js:597, :599). request() for reports is serialized by state.busy/again.
title: An older Default range read can overwrite a newer one
trigger: 1. Open the panel; firstLoad starts settings.get. 2. Change Default range in Settings before it answers; onDidChange starts a second get. 3. The second answers first, then the first answers with the old value.
